rv.q: Joanna Parker’s set design quietly supports a play that hangs in the compelling conversations between its formidable characters.
Unwin’s play gives a brief, humanising insight into a time where care and community were essential to the survival of the people of the United Kingdom.
Clare Burt’s Wilkinson, racking asthmatically across the play, is indelible, crowning the evening in an arc of sacrifice.

cn.t: Critics praise *The Promise* as a timely, compelling political drama. Paul Unwin's homage to Labour MP Ellen Wilkinson resonates strongly, with its post-WWII parallels to modern Britain drawing particular acclaim.
